chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding one in Ihram who shot an antelope and hit it in its hand, causing it to limp from it. He (peace be upon him) said: If the antelope walked upon it and grazed, then upon him is a quarter of its value. And if it went upon its face, so he does not know what it did, then upon him is the redemption (fidyah), because he does not know, perhaps it has perished.

key_terms.لَعَلَّهُ قَدْ هَلَكَ: Perhaps it has perished (uncertainty of death)
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for wounding a wild animal while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *ghurm* (compensation) in Ihram by distinguishing between partial and full liability based on the certainty of the animal's death. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on *istishab* (presumption of continuity) and the precautionary measure (*ihtiyat*) applied when the outcome is ambiguous, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills their spiritual obligations through precise material restitution.
